newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Europe Online relaunches as non-profit group.
newsitem.headline: Europe Online relaunches as non-profit group.

text.p: The former online information service Europe Online SA, which shut down in August after going bankrupt, relaunched itself Tuesday as a non-profit organisation promoting Europe on the Internet.
"Europe Online is now a navigation service, a European gateway to the Internet," new president of the board Candace Johnson told Reuters.

The association, to be called Europe Online Asbl, is sponsored by Luxembourg P&T state telecommunications company and was founded by former Europe Online SA employees. It said Jim Clark, chairman of Netscape Communications Corp., was a member of its advisory board.
Europe Online Asbl said it was providing consumers with a user-friendly interface, easy navigation and information retrieval service for the Internet in various languages.
It does not provide Internet access itself, but acts as a framework for information and content providers in Europe to put their content on the World Wide Web part of the Internet.
Johnson said a number of Internet service providers had shown interest in incorporating Europe Online in their services.
Membership dues and sponsors would finance the association's activities.

"It's going back to the original idea (of Europe Online) which was to inspire and be a catalyst for all those people who were not online, to serve as a standardised platform on which people could put their content," said Johnson, who was previously a board member of Europe Online SA.
The old Luxembourg-based company shut down in mid-August after last-ditch talks with Deutsche Telekom AG and others failed to keep the operation running.

Despite its potential for growth in a burgeoning Internet market, Europe Online SA was plagued by shareholder disagreements over strategy since its formation in 1994 as a European-language alternative to U.S. online services.

With about 25,000 subscribers, the multilingual Europe Online had national services in Germany, Britain and Luxembourg and an international service in English, which included news, weather, travel, sports and entertainment.
Tuesday's relaunch resulted from former supporters and employees of Europe Online SA purchasing the rights to the name, software and service of the company.

In coming weeks the group plans to reinstall some features of the old service, including "Member City," which lets people make home pages on the Internet, and "Chat," a facility to tap into live news from radio stations around the world.

The group said it was providing gateways to the Internet for France, Germany, Britain, Sweden, Netherlands and Luxembourg. It hopes to add Italy, Portugal, Belgium, Finland, Austria and Spain in coming months, followed by the rest of Europe.
The predecessor company succumbed after its biggest shareholder, German publisher Burda Holding GmbH, said in July it was pulling the plug on further funding.
Other shareholders included AT&T Corp., the British publisher Pearson Plc, Luxembourg's Banque et Caisse d'Epargne de l'Etat (BCEE) and Societe Nationale de Credit et d'Investissement (SNCI).
